27768.subject: Physics
27768.question_text: A vehicle of mass m is driven by an engine of power P from rest. Find the minimum time it will take to acquire a speed
27768.explanation:
To find the minimum time \( t \) it takes for a vehicle of mass \( m \) to acquire a speed \( v \) when driven by an engine of power \( P \), we use the work-energy principle. 

The relationship is given by:
\(t = \frac{m v^2}{2P}\)

Thus, the minimum time \( t \) to acquire speed \( v \) is:
\(t = \frac{m v^2}{2P}\).

27835.subject: Physics
27835.question_text: A well-lagged bar of length 100cm has its ends maintained at 100oC and 40oC respectively. What is the temperature at a point 60cm from the hotter end?
27835.explanation:
In a well-lagged bar at steady state, temperature decreases linearly with distance

Temperature gradient = \(\frac{\Delta T}{\text{L}}\)

= \(\frac{100 - 40}{100}\) = 0.6º C/cm

Temperature drops at 60cm = 0.6 x 60 = 36º C

Final temperature = 100ºC - 36ºC = 64ºC

41730.question_text: A body of mass 40kg is being dragged along the floor by a rope inclined at 60 degrees to the horizontal. The frictional force between the box and the floor is 100N and the tension on the rope is 300N. How much work is done by dragging the box for a distance of 4m
41730.explanation:
Force required to move the object forward = Fcos 60 = 300 x 0.5 = 150N

Frictional Force = 100N

Total force acting on the object = 150 - 100 = 50N

Work Done = Total force x distance = 50 x 4 = 200J.
